record.ear: Fair and colder. High 35. Low 23. In like a lamb, the Weather Bureau states.

lead.headline: Lasko jury acquits at 3:35 p.m. after hearing the parlour record a second time
lead.deck: Record replayed from 10:01 a.m. to 12:11 p.m.; not guilty on all three counts; the foreman 'heard a man, and could not say which'; the fur coat not found
lead.body: The jury in the trial of Mr. Victor Lasko returned a verdict of not guilty on all three counts at 3:35 p.m. yesterday, after hearing the parlour record of the Hale house a second time in full, from 10:01 a.m. to 12:11 p.m. The foreman, Mr. Arthur Penney of Elmhurst, told Judge Conklin that the jury 'heard a man, and could not say which.' The District Attorney will not proceed further. The fur coat has not been found.

columns.headline: Sergeant Moran finds the fifth tin's cord 'of the same make' as the bag's
columns.body: Detective Sergeant Edward Moran stated yesterday that the waxed cord on the exchange cat's fifth parcel is 'of the same make' as cord in the tool bag of Mr. Joseph Marchetti, held at the 104th Precinct. The make 'is a common one,' he said. The bench warrant remains outstanding.

columns.headline: Newark valve works on two shifts; the sleeve at 1 dollar 05
columns.body: The Newark valve works went to two shifts on Wednesday, the company states, and expects 'ordinary supply' in Queens by the middle of March. The Arcade's hardware counter sold the sleeve yesterday at 1 dollar 05, without limit. Used valves were 25 cents. Eggs are 47 cents.

columns.headline: Inaugural to be carried into 41,000 Queens parlours Monday, Exchange estimates
columns.body: The Queens Exchange estimates that 41,000 parlours in the borough will take the inaugural ceremonies at Washington on Monday by wire, the first inauguration so carried. The Exchange asks subscribers not to place calls between 11:30 a.m. and 2 p.m. 'except in sickness or fire.'

record.wire: LATE WIRE: Mr. Victor Lasko left the courthouse by the Court Square door at 3:50 p.m. and made no statement.

speaker.ear: Fair and colder. High 35. March came in like a lamb. Lambs are not guilty either.

lead.headline: Jury gives the parlour a second hearing, and Lasko walks off the record
lead.deck: Not guilty three times at twenty-five to four; the foreman heard a man and could not say which; the coat remains at large and is wanted for questioning
lead.body: Twelve men sat through four hours and twenty minutes of the Hale parlour, the clock, the dog, the window and the four words, twice over, and at twenty-five to four yesterday they told Judge Conklin they had heard a man and could not say which. Not guilty, three times. Mr. Lasko put on his hat and went home to Corona. The parlour has not commented. The coat is still at large, and is the only party to the case nobody has heard from.

columns.headline: Party Line's string matches the bag, and the Sergeant won't pull it
columns.body: Sergeant Moran says the cord on Party Line's fifth tin is the same make as the cord in Marchetti's unclaimed tool bag at the 104th. He adds that it is a common make. Every lineman in Queens owns some. Party Line owns five lengths, and is not talking.

columns.headline: Ask the Operator: 'May I ring my mother during the inauguration?'
columns.body: Madam, the Exchange asks that nobody ring between half past eleven and two on Monday except for sickness or fire. The operator suggests you tell your mother you are on fire. She will be so relieved when you are not that she will forget to mention the other thing.

columns.headline: Valves come off the high shelf as Newark doubles up the line
columns.body: The Newark works have gone to two shifts and the sleeve is a dollar five at the Arcade, no limit. In January it was a dollar forty-five and a fistfight. The pawnbroker on Jackson Avenue is now selling used valves only to people who want to hear old news.

speaker.wire: LATE WIRE: Juror Penney of Elmhurst says he is switching his own parlour off tonight. For Lent. Also for good.

record.ear: Cloudy. High 40. Low 30. Rain likely at Washington on Monday, the Bureau states.

lead.headline: Exchange to hold all Queens trunk lines to Washington from 11:30 a.m. Monday
lead.deck: Inaugural ceremonies to be carried into parlours from the Capitol; operators on double watch; the oath to be taken down by the house systems of 212 public buildings
lead.body: The Queens Exchange will hold its trunk lines to Washington open from 11:30 a.m. Monday until the end of the inaugural parade, Superintendent Wilfred Arne announced yesterday, so that the ceremonies at the Capitol may be heard in an estimated 41,000 parlours in the borough. Operators will work a double watch. The oath, to be administered to Mr. Hoover by Chief Justice Taft, will also be taken down by the house systems of 212 public buildings. The Weather Bureau forecasts rain at Washington.

columns.headline: Week's count: 23 horses down since December; nine lame in the thaw's ruts
columns.body: The Long Island City carters' association counts 23 horses down on ice in Queens since December, one more than at the Woodside meeting, and nine lame this week in the ruts left by the thaw. The Transit Commission has not answered the carters' letter. Their deadline is March 15.

columns.headline: Commission names Mr. Aldous Venn engineer for the Astoria works
columns.body: The Public Service Commission yesterday named Mr. Aldous Venn, of its Albany staff, as the engineer who will enter the Astoria works of Queens Light & Power by April 1 with an instrument 'not of the company's make.' Alderman Feeney's request to bring the terrier Duke is under consideration.

columns.headline: Greenpoint householders report the tone on four nights this week
columns.body: The Greenpoint petitioners report the tone between midnight and 4 a.m. on four of the past seven nights, Mr. Walter Szabo, their secretary, states. The Brooklyn Borough President's office has referred the complaint to the Public Service Commission, which has referred it to Queens.

record.wire: LATE WIRE: Mr. Victor Lasko returned to work at the Corona gasworks at 7 a.m. yesterday, the works superintendent states.

speaker.ear: Cloudy. High 40. Washington expects rain. Washington usually gets what it expects.

lead.headline: Queens clears the line for Hoover, and asks the neighbours to hold
lead.deck: Exchange holds every trunk to Washington from half past eleven Monday; 41,000 parlours to hear the oath; operators on double watch and double coffee
lead.body: On Monday, for the first time since Washington was a man and not a town, a President will be sworn in where the whole country can hear him do it. The Exchange will hold the Washington trunks open from half past eleven and asks Queens not to ring anybody, for anything, until two. Forty-one thousand parlours will be listening. The operators, who will hear it whether they like it or not, are working double. Bring an umbrella to your parlour. It is raining there.

columns.headline: The Listening Lady: Kew Gardens sets a place at table for the oath
columns.body: Darlings, a Kew Gardens hostess has invited forty to luncheon on Monday to hear Mr. Hoover take the oath, with a chair at the head of the table left empty for the President. Guests are asked not to chew during the oath. Soup will be served after.

columns.headline: Albany names the man to take the Hum's pulse, and Duke wants a second opinion
columns.body: Mr. Aldous Venn of the Commission's Albany staff will go into the Astoria works by April with a meter not of the company's make. Alderman Feeney still wants to bring Duke of 31st Street. The Commission is considering the dog. The dog is considering the Commission.

columns.headline: Where's WORS? Pike rigs a fourth launch, and readers send in their sums
columns.body: Mr. Pike has stationed a fourth launch off North Beach for the next time WORS reads its figures. Our readers have now sent in twenty-five sets of the figures they heard, and fourteen of them have added theirs up. No two totals agree. All are pinned.

speaker.wire: LATE WIRE: Lasko went back to the gasworks yesterday. The coat did not report for work.

editorial.headline: She gave up nothing for Lent
editorial.body: The clergy of Queens have been asked by this paper to denounce the woman called Lilith from their pulpits this Lent. We regret to report the replies. Father Daly of St. Rita's says he will denounce her when she stops paying his parishioners' coal bills. The Reverend Mrs. Hollis of the Methodist mission says she has never met Lilith and wishes she had. Rabbi Stern says Lilith in the old stories was the first woman who would not lie down for Adam, and that he does not see a sin in it. We print these letters because we are fair. We publish this editorial because we are right, and because somebody in this borough must be.

lead.headline: Listening Act returns to the Assembly Tuesday with the Burkhardt amendment
lead.deck: Third reading at 11 a.m.; amendment admits the record of a death in any proceeding; the Real Estate Owners' Association takes 40 gallery seats; the Clerk's machine at the door
lead.body: The Listening Act will be read a third time in the Assembly at 11 a.m. Tuesday, Assemblyman Thomas Burkhardt's office stated last night, with his amendment admitting the record of a death in any proceeding. The Real Estate Owners' Association has taken 40 seats in the gallery, Mr. Ambrose Tully confirmed. Visitors to the gallery will again be asked to speak a word into the Clerk's machine at the door, the Clerk stating that the voice heard on January 22 'has not yet been found among them.'

columns.headline: Stations of the Cross to be carried by telephone from nine Queens parishes
columns.body: Nine Queens parishes will carry the Stations of the Cross by telephone on Friday evenings through Lent for the sick and housebound, the Chancery states, subscribers ringing before 7:30 p.m. The operators, who 'hear by their duty,' are not bound to silence.

columns.headline: Phonautograph Society to record the inaugural in three Queens parlours
columns.body: The Phonautograph Society of Queens will record the inaugural ceremonies tomorrow in three parlours, in Flushing, Jamaica and Long Island City, 'so that 1978 may compare how the oath was heard,' Mr. Cyril Abbot states. The masters will go into the fifth copper case.

columns.headline: President signs the Jones Law; penalties to five years and 10,000 dollars
columns.body: President Coolidge yesterday signed the Jones Law, raising the penalty for a first offence against the Prohibition Act to five years' imprisonment and a fine of 10,000 dollars, Washington states. Inspector Arthur Kane of the Queens police states that instructions to the precincts in the borough are unchanged.

record.wire: LATE WIRE: The Exchange reports 1,140 calls to Washington booked for Monday before 11:30 a.m.

speaker.ear: Rain. High 44. Sunday. The Speaker is resting its voice for Monday.

lead.headline: No tin for Party Line this Friday, and the exchange cat is left on hold
lead.deck: Five Fridays of sardines from Corona, then nothing; she waits by the parcel window till half past five; the operators buy her a tin with the wrong string
lead.body: For five Fridays the parcel post brought a tin of sardines to Party Line, the exchange cat of Position 43, postmarked Corona and tied with lineman's cord. This Friday it brought nothing. Party Line sat by the parcel window from four until half past five, then went and sat on the warm end of the board, where the Corona calls come in, and stayed there. The operators bought her a tin at the Arcade. She has not touched it. It came with the wrong string.

columns.headline: Albany calls the Act for Tuesday, and the Clerk's machine keeps an ear out
columns.body: The Listening Act gets its third reading at eleven on Tuesday, Burkhardt amendment and all. Mr. Tully has forty gallery seats. Every visitor will say a word into the Clerk's machine at the door, in case one of them is the voice. None of them has been yet.

columns.headline: Society will bottle the oath three ways, for a future fond of comparisons
columns.body: The Phonautograph Society will take down tomorrow's oath in three parlours, Flushing, Jamaica and Long Island City, so that 1978 can compare how Queens heard it. Mr. Abbot says the difference will be instructive. We say it will be the furniture.

columns.headline: Ask the Operator: 'Will the President hear me listening?'
columns.body: Sir, no. The line runs one way on Monday, from the Capitol to your parlour. The President will hear only the Chief Justice, the rain and the Senate. The operator, however, will hear everything, and asks you to sit still.

speaker.wire: LATE WIRE: Eleven hundred and forty calls to Washington booked for tomorrow morning, chiefly, the operators suspect, from people wishing to say they were listening.

record.ear: Cloudy. High 41. Low 33. Rain at Washington through the afternoon.

lead.headline: Mr. Hoover takes the oath at the Capitol today; schools and courts to hear it
lead.deck: Chief Justice Taft to administer the oath on the east portico; public schools assemble at 11:45 a.m.; the County Court recesses from noon to 1; Exchange trunks held from 11:30 a.m.
lead.body: Mr. Herbert Hoover will take the oath of office today from Chief Justice Taft on the east portico of the Capitol, and Mr. Coolidge will leave office at the same hour. The public schools of Queens will assemble at 11:45 a.m. to hear the ceremonies over their house systems, the Board of Education states, and the County Court will recess from noon to 1. The Queens Exchange holds its Washington trunks from 11:30 a.m. The Weather Bureau forecasts rain at Washington through the afternoon.

columns.headline: Athletic Club five close the season beating the Bayonne Elks 29 to 24
columns.body: The Long Island City Athletic Club five closed the season at the armory on Saturday night, beating the Bayonne Elks 29 to 24 before 2,100. Mr. Frank Dillon scored 12. The club finishes with twelve wins and eight losses. St. John's Hospital heard all twenty games by wire.

columns.headline: Yankee pitchers and catchers at work at St. Petersburg; workouts recorded
columns.body: The Yankee pitchers and catchers worked out at St. Petersburg on Saturday, the club's operator reports, and Manager Miller Huggins has ordered the workouts recorded 'for the pitchers' benefit.' The remainder of the squad reports during the week.

columns.headline: Second Jamaica marathon to open April 6; 31 couples entered
columns.body: The Jamaica Arena's second dance marathon will open on April 6 at 8 p.m., to an orchestra playing in three shifts, the management states. Thirty-one couples have entered, among them Mrs. Margaret Corrigan of Hollis, whose partner 'will be named before the night.'

record.wire: LATE WIRE: Rain began at Washington at 2:10 a.m., the Weather Bureau's operator reports.

speaker.ear: Rain at Washington, rain at Queens. High 41. The President is wet through. So are we.

lead.headline: Hoover takes the oath in the rain, and the whole borough hears a throat cleared
lead.deck: Forty-one thousand parlours on the line; Chief Justice Taft swears him in; somebody coughs on the Capitol steps and Queens hears it in its own front room
lead.body: In a cold rain on the east portico today Mr. Hoover put his hand on the Bible, Chief Justice Taft swore him in, and forty-one thousand Queens parlours heard every word. They also heard, between 'faithfully' and 'execute,' a cough. Nobody knows whose. Not the President's, says the President's office. Not the Chief Justice's, says the Chief Justice's. It is now the most famous cough in America, and it belongs to nobody. Mr. Coolidge left by train, without coughing, as far as we could hear.

columns.headline: The Listening Lady: Kew Gardens says 'Bless you' to an empty chair
columns.body: Darlings, the Kew Gardens luncheon heard the oath in perfect silence, the empty chair at the head of the table, until the cough, at which three guests said 'Bless you' to the chair. The hostess has not yet decided whether this was rude, or to whom.

columns.headline: Five years for a highball, and Queens stays on the line for last orders
columns.body: On his last Saturday in office Mr. Coolidge signed the Jones Law: five years and ten thousand dollars for what was a fine on Friday. Queens read it twice and ordered another near beer. The 109th Precinct says its instructions have not changed, which is what has always been so good about them.

columns.headline: Exchange holds the line for Washington, and Queens holds its tongue
columns.body: From half past eleven to two the Exchange carried Washington and very little else. Two hundred and six calls came through for sickness, nine for fire and one, at the moment of the oath, from a woman in Ridgewood who wished to know if anybody else had heard the cough.

speaker.wire: LATE WIRE: Our clerk is counting every cough in the whole inaugural. The figure will be printed when he stops coughing.

lead.headline: The oath of office as recorded on the east portico, printed in full
lead.deck: Taken from the Exchange's Washington trunk at Long Island City; 34 seconds; a cough after 'faithfully' attributed by neither the President's office nor the Chief Justice's
lead.body: The oath taken by Mr. Hoover yesterday on the east portico of the Capitol, as recorded on the Exchange's Washington trunk at Long Island City, is printed here in full: 'I do solemnly swear that I will faithfully (a cough) execute the office of President of the United States, and will to the best of my ability, preserve, protect and defend the Constitution of the United States. (Rain.) So help me God.' The oath ran 34 seconds. The cough is not attributed.

columns.headline: Listening Act read a third time in the Assembly at 11 this morning
columns.body: The Assembly takes up the Listening Act for third reading at 11 a.m. today, with Assemblyman Burkhardt's amendment admitting records of a death in any proceeding. Assemblyman Ruel Oakes has filed an amendment exempting farm buildings 'and any barn.'

columns.headline: Fire beneath the Flushing ash dumps north of Corona Avenue; two alarms
columns.body: Fire was found beneath the surface of the Flushing ash dumps north of Corona Avenue at 8:20 p.m. yesterday; two alarms. Battalion Chief Hugh Rennick stated at 11 p.m. that the fire 'is in the ash, not on it,' and may burn for some days.

columns.headline: Inaugural carried to 41,000 parlours without fault; 216 calls placed
columns.body: The Queens Exchange carried the inaugural from 11:30 a.m. to 2:04 p.m. yesterday without fault, Superintendent Wilfred Arne states. In that time 216 calls were placed, 206 for sickness, nine for fire and one 'concerning the cough.' The Exchange made no statement on the cough.

record.wire: LATE WIRE: Smoke from the Flushing dumps reached Elmhurst at 1:10 a.m.; the wind is northwest.

speaker.ear: Clear and colder. High 39. Smoke over Corona. Somebody tell the ash it is Lent.

lead.headline: Assembly turns up the volume and passes the Listening Act, 87 to 59
lead.deck: Burkhardt's amendment carried; Oakes' barn exemption carried too; Mr. Tully's forty landlords leave the gallery in a body; the Senate has it next
lead.body: At twenty to four this afternoon, after four and a half hours, the Assembly passed the Listening Act eighty-seven to fifty-nine, with Mr. Burkhardt's amendment letting a death's record into any court in the State and Mr. Oakes', which exempts barns. Mr. Tully's forty landlords rose in the gallery and left in a body, each saying a word into the Clerk's machine on the way out. None was the voice. The Act goes to the Senate, where Senator Harlan is waiting with his ears shut.

columns.headline: The Speaker counts the coughs: one in the oath, thirty-eight in the address
columns.body: Our clerk sat up with the record of yesterday's ceremonies and counted. There is one cough in the oath, which the Record printed. There are thirty-eight in the address, which the Record did not. Thirty-nine in all, in a cold rain. Bless them.

columns.headline: Flushing's ash heap catches fire, and Corona is all fired up about it
columns.body: The Flushing ash dumps have been burning underneath since last night, two alarms, and the battalion chief says the fire is in the ash, not on it, which is how ash fires prefer it. Corona has taken its washing in. The dumps have been asked to stop.

columns.headline: Ask the Operator: 'Who coughed?'
columns.body: Sir, four hundred and eleven people have asked the operator this since noon yesterday, and she does not know. She has, however, coughed twice herself while answering, and asks that neither be counted.

speaker.wire: LATE WIRE: Senator Harlan says the Senate will take up the Act 'when it is quiet enough to hear anything.'

record.ear: Fair. High 42. Low 30. Smoke over Corona and Elmhurst.

lead.headline: Assembly passes the Listening Act 87 to 59 with the Burkhardt amendment
lead.deck: Vote at 3:40 p.m. after four hours 30 minutes; farm buildings exempted on the Oakes amendment; the bill referred to the Senate Judiciary Committee
lead.body: The Assembly passed the Listening Act at 3:40 p.m. yesterday by 87 votes to 59, after four hours 30 minutes of debate. Assemblyman Burkhardt's amendment admitting the record of a death in any proceeding was carried 80 to 66, and Assemblyman Oakes' amendment exempting farm buildings 'and any barn' by voice. The bill goes to Senator Edmund Harlan's Judiciary Committee. Forty members of the Real Estate Owners' Association left the gallery during the vote. None matched the voice of January 22.

columns.headline: Ash dump fire burns a second day; Corona house systems record a crackling
columns.body: The fire beneath the Flushing ash dumps burned through yesterday across about four acres, Battalion Chief Hugh Rennick states. Householders on 108th Street, Corona, report that their house systems took down 'a crackling, like frying,' through the night. The Sanitation Department is bringing water by cart.

columns.headline: Valves fall to 98 cents the sleeve, first price under a dollar since January
columns.body: The sleeve of receiving valves fell to 98 cents at the Vantry Arcade yesterday, the first price under a dollar since the Newark fire of January, the hardware counterman reports. Used valves were 20 cents on Jackson Avenue. Eggs are 48 cents, Lent having raised them.

columns.headline: Commission engineer to enter Astoria works March 28; the dog declined
columns.body: The Public Service Commission states that Mr. Aldous Venn will enter the Astoria works of Queens Light & Power on March 28 at 9 a.m. The Commission has declined Alderman Feeney's request that the terrier Duke accompany him, 'the order naming one instrument.'

record.wire: LATE WIRE: Senator Harlan said at Albany at 6 p.m. that the Judiciary Committee 'will hear the Act in its turn.'

speaker.ear: Fair. High 42. Corona smells of Tuesday's ashes. It is Lent all week in Corona.

lead.headline: Flushing's ash dumps catch fire, and Corona's parlours start to crackle
lead.deck: Four acres burning under the surface; 108th Street's house systems record a frying sound all night; the Sanitation men bring water by the cart, and the fire drinks it
lead.body: The fire under the Flushing ash dumps is in its second day and its fourth acre, and nobody can get at it, because it is under the ash, which is on top of it. The Sanitation men pour water from carts. The ash drinks it and smokes. On 108th Street the house systems recorded all night, as they do, and when the householders played back this morning they heard a crackling, like bacon. Corona has given up meat for Lent. It is being made to listen to it instead.

columns.headline: Albany's Act goes up to the Senate, and Harlan puts it on hold
columns.body: The Listening Act passed the Assembly eighty-seven to fifty-nine and has gone to the Senate, where Senator Harlan says his committee will hear it in its turn. The Senator did not say whose turn. His committee room, we note, has no house system. He had it taken out.

columns.headline: Duke is barred from the works, and the Alderman bares his teeth
columns.body: The Commission says Mr. Venn goes into the Astoria works on March 28 and Duke of 31st Street does not, the order naming one instrument. Alderman Feeney says he will appeal on the dog's behalf. Duke has been told. He went and lay down facing Astoria.

columns.headline: Valves dip under a dollar, and the Arcade counter is all ears
columns.body: The sleeve of valves went to ninety-eight cents at the Arcade yesterday, under a dollar for the first time since Newark burned. Eggs went up to forty-eight. In Lent a sleeve of valves is now cheaper than an omelette, and lasts longer.

speaker.wire: LATE WIRE: A reader in Woodhaven makes the inaugural coughs forty, not thirty-nine. He is coming in to listen.

record.ear: Cloudy. High 45. Low 34. Smoke over Corona.

lead.headline: Ash dump fire spreads to six acres; Corona house systems record a third night
lead.deck: Battalion Chief Rennick: the fire 'twelve feet down'; 30 water carts; windows to be kept shut on 108th and 111th Streets; householders' records offered to the Health Department
lead.body: The fire beneath the Flushing ash dumps had spread to about six acres at 6 p.m. yesterday and was burning 'twelve feet down,' Battalion Chief Hugh Rennick stated. Thirty water carts of the Sanitation Department worked through the day. The Health Department advised householders on 108th and 111th Streets, Corona, to keep their windows shut. Eleven householders offered the Department the records of their house systems for the past three nights, in which a crackling is heard throughout. The Department said it 'does not require them.'

columns.headline: Dr. Strand posts the WORS 1610 carol to Aberystwyth in 22 bars
columns.body: Dr. Matthias Strand of Union Seminary posted yesterday to the National Library of Wales at Aberystwyth a written copy of the carol heard on WORS 1610, in 22 bars, with a note that it is 'written as nearly as it can be, and not nearly enough.'

columns.headline: Senate Judiciary Committee sets no date for the Listening Act
columns.body: Senator Edmund Harlan's Judiciary Committee met at Albany yesterday for 40 minutes and set no date for hearing the Listening Act. Assemblyman Burkhardt said he would 'sit outside the committee room until it does.' He sat there from 3 p.m. until 6.

columns.headline: Byrd's ships 300 miles from Dunedin; the sun lower at Little America
columns.body: The City of New York reported at 9:30 p.m. Tuesday that she was 300 miles from Dunedin. Little America sent 'all well, 24 below, sun at noon now low over the barrier.' The messages were played in the Record's window to 190.

record.wire: LATE WIRE: Detective Sergeant Edward Moran visited the Queens Exchange at 4 p.m. and spoke with the supervisor of Position 43.

speaker.ear: Cloudy. High 45. Smoke over Corona, with a crackle on top.

lead.headline: Sergeant calls at the Exchange, and Party Line won't put him through
lead.deck: Moran spends forty minutes at Position 43 asking who brings the tins; the supervisor says the parcel post; the cat says nothing and sits on his hat
lead.body: Sergeant Moran of the 104th spent forty minutes yesterday afternoon at the Queens Exchange, asking the supervisor of Position 43 about the five tins of sardines that have come for Party Line by parcel post. Who sent them, he asked. The parcel post, she said. Who at the parcel post, he asked. She said she connects calls, not sardines. Party Line, asleep on his hat, woke, looked at him for a long time and went back to sleep. He left without the hat. Then he came back for it.

columns.headline: Ash fire digs in twelve feet, and Corona plays it back with feeling
columns.body: Six acres now, twelve feet down, thirty water carts. Eleven Corona families offered the Health Department their house records of three nights' crackling. The Department said it did not require them. The families say they did not require the crackling either.

columns.headline: Burkhardt camps in Harlan's hallway, and the Senate leaves him on hold
columns.body: Mr. Burkhardt sat on a bench outside Senator Harlan's committee room from three until six yesterday, waiting for a date for the Listening Act. The committee met for forty minutes and set none. The bench, we are told, was very attentive.

columns.headline: Where's WORS? Pin ninety-five comes in over the President
columns.body: A Steinway reader was playing back the inaugural record on Monday night at ten to three, she writes, when WORS came in over it reading figures. She says the President was not interrupted and neither was WORS. Pin ninety-five. Mr. Pike's fourth launch heard nothing.

speaker.wire: LATE WIRE: The Woodhaven reader counted the coughs with our clerk today. They now agree on thirty-nine. The reader had counted a sneeze.

lead.headline: Newark works to restore valves to December's price by March 20, company states
lead.deck: Third shift from Monday; the sleeve at 92 cents at the Arcade against 1 dollar 45 on February 1; used valves 15 cents on Jackson Avenue, where two dealers have closed
lead.body: The Newark valve works will put on a third shift from Monday and expects receiving valves to return 'to the price of last December' by March 20, the company stated yesterday. The sleeve sold at 92 cents at the Vantry Arcade's hardware counter, against 1 dollar 45 on February 1. Used valves were 15 cents on Jackson Avenue, where two dealers have closed. Mr. Jacob Fass of the Arcade counter states that customers 'buy one sleeve again, not six.' Eggs are 49 cents.

columns.headline: Mr. Gorman's counsel files a 46-page brief on the Riverhead seal
columns.body: Counsel for Mr. Francis Gorman filed at the Appellate Division yesterday a brief of 46 pages on the Board of Elections' seal on 11 seconds of its Riverhead record, to be argued March 18. The Board will reply on Monday. The warrant for Mr. Joseph Marchetti, lineman, is outstanding.

columns.headline: Ash fire 'under control but not out' on its fourth day
columns.body: Battalion Chief Hugh Rennick stated at 5 p.m. yesterday that the Flushing ash dump fire is 'under control but not out,' and that the department will trench around six acres. Corona householders report the crackling on their systems 'fainter, but there.' Smoke reached Jackson Heights at noon.

columns.headline: Phonautograph Society meets tonight on record No. 23; committee at 14 and 14
columns.body: The Phonautograph Society of Queens meets at 8 tonight at its Jamaica office on Mrs. Ottoline Grieve's third motion that record No. 23, the Maspeth party's midnight record, be played to members. The committee stands at 14 and 14, Mr. Cyril Abbot holding the chair and its casting vote.

record.wire: LATE WIRE: Mr. Victor Lasko applied at 3 p.m. yesterday to the County Clerk for the return of his overcoat, held as an exhibit.

speaker.ear: Milder. High 50. Spring is on the line. Hold, please.

lead.headline: Newark works the night shift, and the price of valves loses its glow
lead.deck: Ninety-two cents the sleeve at the Arcade; a third shift from Monday; Jackson Avenue's used-valve men shut up shop, and one of them goes into eggs
lead.body: In January a sleeve of valves cost a dollar forty-five, and men stood in line at the Arcade at seven in the morning with their wives' egg money. Today a sleeve is ninety-two cents, Newark is putting on a third shift, and the price will be December's by the twentieth. The two used-valve dealers of Jackson Avenue have closed. One has gone into eggs, which are forty-nine cents and rising for Lent. He says eggs break quieter.

columns.headline: Lasko asks for his overcoat back, and the D.A. finds it hard to let go
columns.body: Mr. Lasko applied to the County Clerk yesterday afternoon for the return of his own overcoat, held as an exhibit since January. The Clerk says it will take a week. The other coat, the fur, was never an exhibit, because nobody has ever found it. It is still nobody's.

columns.headline: The Society votes tonight on No. 23, and Abbot holds the casting call
columns.body: Fourteen for, fourteen against, and Mr. Abbot in the chair with the casting vote, which he has twice used against hearing record No. 23 of the Maspeth party. Mrs. Grieve moves a third time at eight tonight. She is bringing her own chair.

columns.headline: Ask the Operator: 'Is it spring yet?'
columns.body: Madam, the operator cannot say, but she reports that the first call this morning asking whether it was spring came at seven minutes past six from Kissena Park, from a man who wished it known that he had heard something in a tree.

speaker.wire: LATE WIRE: Dr. Strand has posted the WORS carol to Wales in twenty-two bars. He says there is a twenty-third that will not go on paper.

lead.headline: Phonautograph Society divides 14 to 14 on record No. 23; Mr. Abbot votes no
lead.deck: Meeting at the Jamaica office from 8:05 p.m. to 11:50 p.m.; the casting vote given a third time; Mrs. Grieve resigns from the committee and gives notice of a fourth motion
lead.body: The Phonautograph Society of Queens divided 14 to 14 at 11:40 p.m. yesterday on Mrs. Ottoline Grieve's motion that record No. 23, made at a Maspeth party at midnight, be played to members, and Mr. Cyril Abbot, in the chair, gave his casting vote against it, as on two earlier occasions. Mrs. Grieve resigned from the committee at 11:45 p.m. and gave notice of a fourth motion for April. Mr. Abbot stated that the record 'remains in the Society's keeping, unplayed.' The meeting was recorded.

columns.headline: Week's count: ash fire trenched on six acres after five days; 212 cartloads
columns.body: The Flushing ash dump fire was in its fifth day last night, Battalion Chief Hugh Rennick reporting six acres trenched and the fire 'under control but not out,' 212 cartloads of water used, three firemen treated for smoke. Corona householders report the crackling on their systems at night only.

columns.headline: First robin of the season recorded at Kissena Park at 6:07 a.m.
columns.body: The first robin of the season was recorded at Kissena Park at 6:07 a.m. yesterday by Mr. Emmett Lowry of the Queens Bird Club, who had left a set in a sycamore. The record runs 1 minute 12 seconds. Last year's first robin was recorded March 14.

columns.headline: Commission to hear the Greenpoint petitioners on April 2
columns.body: The Public Service Commission has agreed to hear the Greenpoint petitioners on April 2, after its engineer has entered the Astoria works, Mr. Walter Szabo, their secretary, states. The tone was reported in Greenpoint on five nights this week, between midnight and 3:50 a.m.

record.wire: LATE WIRE: Mrs. Ottoline Grieve left the Jamaica office at 11:52 p.m. carrying the record of the meeting, which she said she would return 'when played.'

speaker.ear: Fair and mild. High 53. A robin was heard in Flushing. Not by us.

lead.headline: Abbot breaks the tie again, and record No. 23 stays off the record
lead.deck: Fourteen to fourteen at twenty to midnight in Jamaica; Mrs. Grieve resigns from the committee, takes the minutes home and promises April
lead.body: For the third time of asking, the Phonautograph Society of Queens has voted fourteen to fourteen on whether to listen to record No. 23, and for the third time Mr. Abbot has broken the tie by not listening. The record, made at a party in Maspeth at midnight, stays in the Society's cupboard, unheard by anybody now living. Mrs. Grieve resigned from the committee at a quarter to twelve taking the record of the meeting with her. She says she will bring it back when they play hers.

columns.headline: Week's count: thirty-nine coughs, final, and we stand by every one
columns.body: After four days, one reader from Woodhaven and a great many lozenges, the Speaker's count of the inaugural coughs is closed at thirty-nine, one in the oath and thirty-eight in the address. The Record has printed one. We stand by all thirty-nine.

columns.headline: A robin turns up on the record in Kissena Park, and spring is on the line
columns.body: Mr. Lowry of the Queens Bird Club left a recording set up a sycamore in Kissena Park for a week, and yesterday at seven minutes past six it took down a robin, a minute and twelve seconds. He played it to the Club last night. They asked for it again.

columns.headline: Where's WORS? Pike's fourth launch gets cold feet off North Beach
columns.body: Mr. Pike's fourth launch sat off North Beach five nights this week and heard nothing but the ash fire, faintly, on its own receiver. WORS has been quiet since Monday. The pins stand at ninety-five. Our office boy has been told to stop dusting them.

speaker.wire: LATE WIRE: Mrs. Grieve has the minutes. Mr. Abbot has the record. Jamaica has never been so thoroughly documented.

editorial.headline: Twelve good women and true, and no law to let them
editorial.body: No woman in New York may sit on a jury, the Legislature having decided that jury rooms are no place for the gentler sex. On Monday, as the nation inaugurated a President whose cough was recorded for posterity, twelve women sat in the borough hall rotunda in borrowed robes and tried the State for contempt of half its citizens. They heard the evidence, played back from the Legislature's own records, and found the State guilty in eleven minutes. A black silk thread was tied around the gavel. This was a farce, and the Speaker reports it as one. We note, however, that it was the shortest trial in the borough's history and that nobody has yet appealed the verdict.

record.ear: Cloudy, showers by night. High 51. Low 40.

lead.headline: All twelve screws on the Arcade's lien notices of the Vantry & Co. pattern
lead.deck: Borough hardware inspector examines the north door at Mr. Haas's request; pattern 'not made since 1924'; Signal Ground Rents Inc. rung three times without answer
lead.body: The Borough's hardware inspector, Mr. Lyle Danforth, examined at Mr. Ludwig Haas's request yesterday all twelve steel screws holding the three lien notices on the Vantry Arcade's north door, and reported each of them to be of a Vantry & Co. pattern 'not made since 1924.' The notices were posted in November, December and February. Signal Ground Rents Inc., which posted them, did not answer its telephone at 10 a.m., 2 p.m. or 4 p.m. The screws were replaced.

columns.headline: Stations of the Cross by telephone heard by 3,100 subscribers, Chancery states
columns.body: The Stations of the Cross carried by telephone on Friday evening from nine Queens parishes were heard by about 3,100 subscribers, chiefly the sick and housebound, the Chancery states. The Chancery thanks the operators, 'who heard by their duty and were not bound.'

columns.headline: Arcade toy shop's two dolls found facing the shop a second time
columns.body: The proprietress of the Vantry Arcade's toy shop reports that the two answering dolls on the back shelf were found on Friday morning facing the shop, as on February 25, after being turned to face the wall at closing on Thursday. She has moved them to a drawer.

columns.headline: City of New York reported 120 miles from Dunedin; Little America 'well'
columns.body: The City of New York reported at 9:15 p.m. Friday that she was 120 miles from Dunedin. Little America sent 'all well, 31 below, the sun below the barrier at 9:10 p.m.' Played in the Record's window to 230.

record.wire: LATE WIRE: The fire beneath the Flushing ash dumps was reported 'smouldering, three acres' at 10 p.m.

speaker.ear: Showers by night. High 51. Sunday. The robin is resting. So is the Speaker.

lead.headline: Spring rings in at Kissena Park, and a robin cuts its first record
lead.deck: Mr. Lowry's sycamore set takes down seventy-two seconds of song; the Bird Club plays it four times; a quarrel breaks out over whether it is last year's robin
lead.body: Every March somebody in Queens hears the first robin, and every March somebody else says he heard it first. This year Mr. Emmett Lowry of Flushing has the record, a minute and twelve seconds taken down by a set he hid in a sycamore in Kissena Park, at seven past six on Friday morning. The Bird Club has played it four times. Two members say it is last year's robin, back. One says it is last year's record, played back. Mr. Lowry is not arguing. He is up the tree.

columns.headline: The Arcade's screws all turn out one make, and the landlord still won't pick up
columns.body: Mr. Haas had all twelve screws in his three lien notices looked at yesterday. All twelve are Vantry & Co., a pattern nobody has made since 1924. Signal Ground Rents was rung at ten, two and four. It let every call ring out. We admire its consistency.

columns.headline: The toy shop's dolls do an about-turn, and go into a drawer for it
columns.body: The two answering dolls in the Arcade toy shop were turned to the wall at closing on Thursday and found facing the shop on Friday morning, for the second time. The proprietress has shut them in a drawer. She says the drawer faces nowhere.

columns.headline: Ask the Operator: 'Does the ash fire have a number?'
columns.body: Sir, it does not, though eleven Corona families have rung the Exchange to ask that it be disconnected. The operator has explained that she can only disconnect what she connected. The ash fire, she says, connected itself.

speaker.wire: LATE WIRE: Corona reports the crackle fainter tonight. The ash is down to a whisper. We have asked it to speak up.

lead.headline: Transit Commission silent four days before the carters' March 15 deadline
lead.deck: Association's letter of February 22 unanswered; 'no ice and no coal beneath the structure' from 6 a.m. Friday; ice companies to serve Roosevelt Avenue by the side streets
lead.body: The Transit Commission has not answered the letter of the Long Island City carters' association of February 22, asking that Roosevelt Avenue be sanded beneath the elevated each morning and the structure's drip repaired, Mr. Dennis Rafferty, the association's secretary, stated yesterday. Unless an answer is received by Friday, he said, no member will carry ice or coal beneath the structure from 6 a.m. that day. The Corona and Bowery Bay ice companies are arranging to serve the avenue from the side streets. Twenty-four horses have now fallen.

columns.headline: Yankee squad complete at St. Petersburg; batting practice recorded daily
columns.body: The Yankee squad completed its reporting at St. Petersburg on Saturday, Manager Miller Huggins stating that batting practice will be recorded each day 'so that a man may hear his own swing.' Babe Ruth batted for 40 minutes before about 1,200.

columns.headline: Flushing ash dump fire smouldering on three acres in its seventh day
columns.body: The Flushing ash dump fire was smouldering on three acres at 6 p.m. yesterday, its seventh day, Battalion Chief Hugh Rennick states. The crackling on the house systems of Corona was reported by four householders on Saturday night and by one on Sunday.

columns.headline: Board of Elections files its reply today in Mr. Gorman's appeal
columns.body: The Board of Elections files its reply this morning to Mr. Francis Gorman's brief in the appeal on the sealed 11 seconds of its Riverhead record, to be argued before the Appellate Division a week today. The warrant for Mr. Joseph Marchetti remains outstanding.

record.wire: LATE WIRE: WORS 1610 was heard in Woodside at 7:40 p.m. yesterday, earlier in the evening than any previous report, the Radio Division states.

speaker.ear: Fair. High 48. The carters give the El till Friday. The El gives nothing.

lead.headline: WORS signs on early in Woodside, and a little girl gets a word in
lead.deck: Twenty to eight Sunday evening; a girl of seven on 61st Street says goodnight to the set; the figures stop; the house takes down the rest, and Mr. Pike has it now
lead.body: WORS has never been heard before midnight. On Sunday at twenty to eight it came on in a front room on 61st Street, Woodside, reading its figures, while a girl of seven was being put to bed. She said goodnight to the set, as she does to the cat. The figures stopped. Then a voice said one word. Her mother says the word was goodnight. Her father says it was not. The house took it all down, and Mr. Pike has the record. He is not saying either.

columns.headline: Yankees swing into camp, and Huggins records every one
columns.body: The Yankees are all in camp at St. Petersburg and Mr. Huggins is recording every swing, so that each man may hear what he did wrong. The Babe hit for forty minutes on Saturday before twelve hundred. Mr. Huggins does not need to play the Babe's back.

columns.headline: Carters give the El till Friday, and the Commission's line is dead
columns.body: The carters' letter to the Transit Commission is seventeen days old and unanswered. On Friday at six the ice and coal stop going under the elevated, and the ice companies will come round by the side streets. The horses, consulted at last, are in favour.

columns.headline: The ash fire burns low, and Corona's parlours can hear themselves think
columns.body: Seven days in, the Flushing ash fire is down to three acres and a smoulder, and only one Corona house recorded any crackling on Sunday night. The householder says he misses it. His wife says he is the only one who does.

speaker.wire: LATE WIRE: The girl on 61st Street has been put to bed with the set switched off. She says it was rude not to answer.

lead.headline: Radio Division receives a Woodside house record of WORS 1610 made Sunday
lead.deck: Transmission of 2 minutes 50 seconds in a front room on 61st Street; figures read in fours, a child's 'Goodnight,' then one word not transcribed; 'the first report before midnight'
lead.body: Mr. Harold Pike of the Radio Division stated yesterday that the Division has the record made by a house system on 61st Street, Woodside, at 7:40 p.m. Sunday, in which WORS 1610 is heard for 2 minutes 50 seconds. A man's voice reads figures in groups of four. A child says 'Goodnight.' The figures stop, and after four seconds one word is spoken, which the Division has not transcribed. It is the first report of the station before midnight.

columns.headline: Ash dump fire declared out at 3:20 p.m. after eight days; trench to be watched
columns.body: Battalion Chief Hugh Rennick declared the Flushing ash dump fire out at 3:20 p.m. yesterday, its eighth day, after 340 cartloads of water. The trench will be watched for fourteen days. No crackling was reported by Corona householders on Sunday night after 1 a.m.

columns.headline: Assemblyman Burkhardt asks the Senate committee for a date by March 26
columns.body: Assemblyman Thomas Burkhardt wrote yesterday to Senator Edmund Harlan asking that the Judiciary Committee hear the Listening Act by March 26, the Legislature expecting to adjourn early in April. Senator Harlan's office acknowledged the letter at 4:10 p.m.

columns.headline: Mr. Lasko's overcoat returned to him by the County Clerk at 11 a.m.
columns.body: The County Clerk returned to Mr. Victor Lasko at 11 a.m. yesterday the overcoat held as an exhibit since January. Mr. Lasko signed for it and wore it from the building. The fur coat taken from the Hale house on Christmas Eve has not been found.

record.wire: LATE WIRE: Mr. Hollis Garrity, engineer of the Transit Commission, inspected the elevated structure at Roosevelt Avenue and 74th Street at 2 p.m. and made no statement.

speaker.ear: Cloudy. High 46. The ash fire is out. Corona can hear its own frying again.

lead.headline: Lasko gets his coat back, and the fur is still out in the cold
lead.deck: The County Clerk hands over the overcoat at eleven; Mr. Lasko signs, puts it on and walks out; the other coat, in the Speaker's opinion, has gone south for the winter
lead.body: Yesterday morning at eleven the County Clerk handed Mr. Victor Lasko a brown overcoat, which the State has kept in a box since January as evidence of something. Mr. Lasko signed for it, put it on and walked out into the cold, a free man in a coat. The other coat, the fur from the Hale house, has not been seen since Christmas Eve. It is the only party to the case still not cleared. If it is reading this, the Speaker would like a word.

columns.headline: Pike won't say what WORS said, and Woodside won't talk of anything else
columns.body: Mr. Pike has the 61st Street record and has transcribed everything on it but the last word, which he will not write down. The girl's mother says goodnight. Her father says no. The street has taken sides. The girl has been given a new set of jacks.

columns.headline: The ash fire signs off after eight days, and Corona tunes back in
columns.body: Battalion Chief Rennick declared the Flushing ash fire out yesterday afternoon, after three hundred and forty cartloads of water. Corona's house systems recorded nothing on Sunday night after one. A Corona man played his blank record to his wife this morning to prove it.

columns.headline: Burkhardt writes to Harlan, and asks him please to pick up
columns.body: Mr. Burkhardt has written to Senator Harlan asking for a committee date by March 26, before Albany goes home. The Senator's office acknowledged the letter at ten past four. Acknowledged, in Albany, means somebody held it up to the light.

speaker.wire: LATE WIRE: A Transit Commission engineer looked at the El at Roosevelt and 74th this afternoon. It dripped on him. He made no statement.

lead.headline: Queens Light & Power objects to the instrument its Astoria inspector will carry
lead.deck: Mr. Roland Tisch asks for a meter 'of a make known to the Commission'; Mr. Venn proposes to borrow Dr. Rastin's; Commissioner Lacey to rule Monday
lead.body: Mr. Roland Tisch, counsel for Queens Light & Power, asked the Public Service Commission yesterday to rule that the instrument Mr. Aldous Venn will carry into the company's Astoria works on March 28 be 'of a make known to the Commission.' The Commission's staff disclosed that Mr. Venn proposes to borrow the meter of Dr. Emil Rastin of Columbia, with which the Hum was first measured at 41 cycles. Commissioner Maurice Lacey will rule on Monday. Greenpoint householders reported the tone on three nights last week.

columns.headline: Aberystwyth cables Dr. Strand for 'the bar missing at the end'
columns.body: The National Library of Wales cabled Dr. Matthias Strand yesterday acknowledging the 22 bars of the carol heard on WORS 1610, and asking for 'the bar missing at the end.' Dr. Strand states that he cannot write it down and has offered to sing it by wire.

columns.headline: Mr. Garrity's report on the elevated drip goes to the Transit Commission today
columns.body: Mr. Hollis Garrity, engineer of the Transit Commission, inspected the elevated structure on Roosevelt Avenue between 74th and 82nd Streets on Monday afternoon and will report to the Commission today, his office states. The carters' association has received no answer to its letter.

columns.headline: Second marathon has 44 couples; Mrs. Corrigan names a trombonist partner
columns.body: The Jamaica Arena's second dance marathon, to open April 6, has 44 couples entered, the management states. The orchestra will play in three shifts of eight hours. Mrs. Margaret Corrigan of Hollis has named as her partner Mr. Leo Gant of Woodhaven, a trombonist.

record.wire: LATE WIRE: The tool bag of Mr. Joseph Marchetti was moved at 3 p.m. from the 104th Precinct's property room to the District Attorney's office, Detective Sergeant Edward Moran states.

speaker.ear: Rain. High 47. The light company wants to choose the meter. We want to choose the bill.

lead.headline: Light company wants the meter of its choosing, and Astoria reads the signal
lead.deck: Mr. Tisch objects that Mr. Venn will carry Dr. Rastin's meter into the works, the very one that heard forty-one; Lacey rules Monday; Duke is being kept indoors
lead.body: Last month the Commission ordered the light company to let an engineer into its Astoria works with a meter not of the company's make. Yesterday the company discovered which meter. Mr. Venn proposes to borrow Dr. Rastin's, the one that read forty-one cycles in Astoria, Ditmars and Greenpoint. Mr. Tisch, for the company, wants one 'of a make known to the Commission.' Dr. Rastin says the Commission knows his meter very well, having heard it give evidence for three days. Commissioner Lacey rules on Monday.

columns.headline: Where's WORS? Pin ninety-six, and this one says goodnight
columns.body: Pin ninety-six, 61st Street, Woodside, twenty to eight on a Sunday, is our first pin before midnight, and the first, so far as we know, to be spoken to. We have coloured it red. Readers are asked not to say goodnight to their sets. Several have.

columns.headline: Marchetti's bag moves to the D.A., and the cord goes along on a string
columns.body: The lineman's tool bag that has waited in the 104th's property room since January for Mr. Marchetti to come back for it was carried yesterday to the District Attorney's office. The waxed cord went with it. Party Line has had no tin for two Fridays.

columns.headline: Mrs. Corrigan names her marathon partner, and he's in the band
columns.body: Mrs. Corrigan of Hollis, who outlasted every couple but one at the Arena last month and was then outlasted by a record, has named her partner for April. He is Mr. Leo Gant of Woodhaven, a trombonist. She says it is time she had the band on her side.

speaker.wire: LATE WIRE: Dr. Rastin says his meter has never been inside the works before, and is looking forward to it.

lead.headline: Transit Commission engineer finds the elevated's drip 'within normal limits'
lead.deck: Mr. Garrity's report delivered at 4 p.m.; no sanding recommended; sent to the carters without a letter; the association meets at Woodside Hall at 8 tonight
lead.body: Mr. Hollis Garrity, engineer of the Transit Commission, reported to the Commission at 4 p.m. yesterday that the drip from the elevated structure on Roosevelt Avenue between 74th and 82nd Streets is 'within normal limits for a structure of that age,' and recommended no sanding. The Commission sent the report to the carters' association at 5:30 p.m., without a letter. Mr. Dennis Rafferty, the association's secretary, said the members would meet at Woodside Hall at 8 tonight, and that the resolution of February 21 stands.

columns.headline: Senate Judiciary Committee to hear the Listening Act at 2 p.m. March 27
columns.body: Senator Edmund Harlan announced yesterday that the Judiciary Committee will hear the Listening Act at 2 p.m. on March 27, one day after the date asked by Assemblyman Burkhardt. Mr. Ambrose Tully has asked for one hour. The gallery voice of January 22 has not been identified.

columns.headline: Borden Avenue gates refused a second time, Mr. Stroud reporting
columns.body: The Board of Estimate yesterday refused a second time, 11 votes to 5, the gates at the Borden Avenue crossing, Mr. Warren Stroud reporting 'no change in the circumstances.' The petitioners state they have 4,100 signatures and will not apply a third time before the autumn. The Board's calendar is closed to it until October.

columns.headline: Board asks that its Riverhead seal be kept; Gorman appeal argued Monday
columns.body: The Board of Elections' reply asks the Appellate Division to keep its seal on the 11 seconds of the Riverhead record 'as the Board's own, and nobody's evidence.' Mr. Francis Gorman's appeal will be argued on Monday at 10 a.m. Mr. Joseph Marchetti has not been found.

record.wire: LATE WIRE: The Corona Ice Company states that it will deliver Roosevelt Avenue customers from 75th Street by hand-cart from Friday.

speaker.ear: Colder. High 41. The El says its drip is normal. So is the carters' temper.

lead.headline: El drips 'within normal limits,' and the carters reach theirs
lead.deck: The Commission's engineer looks up, gets wet and recommends nothing; three hundred carters meet tonight in Woodside; tomorrow at six the ice goes round the long way
lead.body: Mr. Garrity of the Transit Commission stood under the elevated on Roosevelt Avenue on Monday, got dripped on, and has now reported that the drip is within normal limits for a structure of its age. He recommends no sand. The carters, twenty-four horses down since December, have read the report, which came without a letter, and meet at eight tonight in Woodside Hall. The resolution stands. From six tomorrow no ice and no coal goes under the El. We shall see who blinks first, and whether horses blink.

columns.headline: Harlan sets the Act for the twenty-seventh, one day late, on the dot
columns.body: Senator Harlan will hear the Listening Act on March 27 at two, the day after Mr. Burkhardt asked. Albany says it is a matter of the calendar. Mr. Burkhardt says it is a matter of Senator Harlan. Mr. Tully has been given an hour, and a glass of water.

columns.headline: Valves back to December's price, and the pawnbrokers ring off
columns.body: Eighty-five cents the sleeve at the Arcade yesterday, December's price, six days before Newark promised it. Nobody on Jackson Avenue will buy a used valve now. One reader writes that he has a drawer of forty. We suggest he listen to them.

columns.headline: The Listening Lady: Forest Hills gives up giving up
columns.body: Darlings, the Forest Hills hostess who resolved to switch her house off from nine to ten each night of Lent switched it on again on Tuesday at nine-forty, having heard, she says, absolutely nothing for three weeks, and needing to know whether anybody had noticed.

speaker.wire: LATE WIRE: The Corona Ice Company will push its ice round from 75th Street by hand-cart. The ice men asked for gloves and a raise. They got gloves.

lead.headline: Carters vote 291 to 14 to stop deliveries beneath the elevated from today
lead.deck: Woodside Hall meeting 8:05 p.m. to 10:40 p.m.; ice and coal to Roosevelt Avenue from the corners by hand; the Transit Commission 'has nothing to add'
lead.body: The Long Island City carters' association voted at Woodside Hall at 10:35 p.m. yesterday, by 291 votes to 14, that from 6 a.m. today no member will carry ice or coal beneath the elevated on Roosevelt Avenue. Mr. Dennis Rafferty said deliveries to the avenue would be made 'from the corners, by hand.' The Transit Commission said at 11 p.m. that it 'has nothing to add to its engineer's report.' The Corona, Bowery Bay and Hallett's Point companies will observe the stoppage.

columns.headline: Mr. Marchetti's tool bag opened at the District Attorney's office
columns.body: Detective Sergeant Edward Moran stated yesterday that the tool bag of Mr. Joseph Marchetti, lineman, was opened at the District Attorney's office and found to contain, besides tools, 'a quantity of waxed lacing cord and an empty sardine tin.' He made no further statement.

columns.headline: Radio Division committee hears the Woodside record of WORS 1610 three times
columns.body: Mr. Harold Pike played the Woodside house record of March 10 to a committee of the Radio Division yesterday, three times. The committee did not transcribe the last word. Mr. Pike said WORS 1610 has not been heard since. The Division's fourth launch remains off North Beach.

columns.headline: Both Byrd ships in port at Dunedin; crews to be heard by wire Sunday
columns.body: Both Byrd ships are at Dunedin, New Zealand, and the crews will be heard by wire from the harbour on Sunday at 9 p.m. Little America sent last night 'all well, 33 below, Jackson in charge.' Played in the Record's window to 210.

record.wire: LATE WIRE: Mr. Francis Gorman's appeal on the Riverhead record will be argued on Monday at 10 a.m. in Brooklyn.

speaker.ear: Fair and cold. High 38. The Ides of March. Beware the El.

lead.headline: Carters cut the El off at six, and Roosevelt Avenue gets its ice by hand
lead.deck: Two hundred and ninety-one to fourteen in Woodside; not a horse under the structure all day; the ice comes round from the corners on hand-carts and the coal comes in buckets
lead.body: At six this morning, on the Ides of March, not a horse went under the elevated on Roosevelt Avenue from Queensboro Plaza to Corona, and not one went all day. The ice came round from the corners on hand-carts, pushed by ice men in new gloves, and the coal came up the side streets in buckets. The El ran on time overhead and dripped on everyone equally. The Transit Commission has nothing to add. The horses had the day off.

columns.headline: Marchetti's bag holds a sardine tin, and Party Line's case smells fishy
columns.body: Sergeant Moran had Mr. Marchetti's tool bag opened at the District Attorney's office yesterday, and found tools, waxed cord and an empty sardine tin. He has made no further statement. Party Line, informed, washed her face. No tin came for her again this Friday, the third.

columns.headline: Where's WORS? Pike plays the goodnight thrice, and the committee sleeps on it
columns.body: Mr. Pike played the Woodside record to the Radio Division's committee three times yesterday. Nobody wrote the last word down. WORS has not been heard since Sunday last. Our readers have sent in nine guesses at the word. We have pinned none of them.

columns.headline: Gorman's appeal comes up Monday, and the Board says its seal is sealed
columns.body: On Monday the Appellate Division hears Mr. Gorman on the eleven sealed seconds of Riverhead. The Board's brief says the record is the Board's own and nobody's evidence. Mr. Gorman says that is what everybody says about a record, until they are on it.

speaker.wire: LATE WIRE: Biddy of the Corona Ice Company was seen at noon looking up at the El. It dripped. She walked on.
